criteria.criterion: Two candidate spans opened within one gate run share a trace id; checked by asserting both against the run span's context.
A candidate span opened INSIDE a `generation._submit_ctx` pool task shares the run span's trace id; checked by submitting the span-opening work through the real `_submit_ctx` and comparing.
Inside a gate run with a recording tracer, `mint_run_identity` returns that run span's trace id rather than a minted value.
A code-review run's candidate spans share one trace id; checked by asserting two of them against each other, proving the third boundary is covered.
With no tracer configured the gate run behaves exactly as before; checked by asserting no exception and an unchanged verdict shape.
With a tracer CONFIGURED that raises on span open, the gate run still completes with an unchanged verdict shape — the failure is swallowed and logged, never propagated.
`gate_dispatch.py` stays at or under the 800-line module cap.

findings.detail: No test in tests/unit/test_run_span.py (or any other test file found) covers the code-review boundary. The test file contains 8 test functions, none of which reference 'code_review', 'code-review', or 'review-code'. The AC explicitly requires asserting two candidate spans from a code-review run against each other to prove the third gate-run boundary (produce_code_review_verdict at :372) is covered. This test is absent.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
